thread.title: Wearables: Apple Maintains Q2 Market Share Lead

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Wearables: Apple Maintains Q2 Market Share Lead
text:
Photo: Fitbit By David Marino-Nachison Sept. 4, 2018 11:44 a.m. ET Fitbit ’s (FIT) slice of overall wearables market share slid in the second quarter, according to new estimates, but the news comes as the company has bolstered its position in smartwatches and announced a new fitness tracker.
The top 5 companies in terms of Q2 wearables shipments—Apple (AAPL), Xiaomi, Fitbit, Huawei and Garmin (GRMN)—were unchanged from Q1 , IDC said Tuesday.
Newsletter Sign-up Apple’s share rose to 17% from 13% year-over-year, IDC said, as Watch demand remained strong. Xiaomi just topped 15%, up from 13.3%, while Fitbit, at 9.5%, slid from 12.8% a year earlier.
Total wearable shipments—the category includes TK—rose 5.5% to 27.9 million from 26.4 million in Q2 2017, according to IDC.
Illustration: IDC “Two key forces were at work during the quarter: stronger demand for smart wearables, and slower declines in the basic wearables market,” IDC’s Ramon Llamas said in a statement . “Users have come to want more from their wearable devices, and smartwatches have met that demand.
More About Barron’s Next Learn more about Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50 Fitbit launched the Versa smartwatch in March; it said it crossed the 1 million shipments threshold back in June. In August, it said its newest tracker, the Charge 3, would arrive in the fall . The company has quickly come to see around half of its revenue come from watches, and it shipped 500,000 more devices in Q2 than in Q1, according to IDC.
“With the launch of the Versa, the fitness giant has successfully expanded its userbase and emerged as the second largest smartwatch brand during the quarter,” IDC wrote. “Fitbit is also one of the few [manufacturers] that continues to actively target the commercial market and remains a market leader in this space.”
Fitbit and Apple are Barron’s Next 50 companies.
